title: Rules and signs
goal: Understand rules and signs, talk to a doctor, and use -mAlY, gerek and bolmak together.

intro.text: Without a subject, `-mAlY` states a rule for everyone: *Bu ýerde aýakgaby çykarmaly*, shoes come off here. Signs often use *gadagan* (forbidden) with an infinitive: *Çilim çekmek gadagan!* And *-mAlY däl* is **mustn't**: *Öýe aýakgap bilen girmeli däl*.

vocab.en: to take off (clothes); to take out

exercises.question: What does the doctor tell Merjen to do?

context.tk: Başym we bogazym agyrýar. Mende gyzzyrma hem bar.
context.en: My head and my throat hurt. I have a fever too.

context.tk: Size sowuk degipdir. Siz üç gün öýde dynç almaly.
context.en: You've caught a cold. You must rest at home for three days.

context.tk: Ýok, gitmeli däl. Bu dermany hem içmeli.
context.en: No, you mustn't. You must take this medicine too.

options: rest at home for three days
go to the pharmacy every day

why.1: *Ýok, gitmeli däl*: she mustn't go to work.
why.2: The doctor says nothing about the pharmacy.

exercises.explain: *Siz üç gün öýde dynç almaly*: you must rest at home for three days.
Signs often say *… gadagan*, forbidden, after an infinitive: *Çilim çekmek gadagan!*

accept: You have to take off your shoes here.
[You must|One must|You should] take off [your|the] shoes here.
[You have to|You must|One must|You should] take [your|the] shoes off here.
You have to take off the shoes here.
Shoes [must|have to] [be taken off|come off] here.

exercises.en: You must be quiet in the hospital.

reject.why: *boluň* is a polite command, **be quiet!** The sentence states a rule: *bolmaly*.

exercises.explain: A rule for everyone: `-mAlY` with no subject, *ýuwaş bolmaly*.

exercises.question: Which sentence is a rule for everyone, not about one person?

why.1: *Men … aýakgabymy* is about **me**: I must take off my shoes.

exercises.explain: With no subject, `-mAlY` states a general rule: shoes come off here.

exercises.label: *gitmek*, questions: must I go?, must you go?… (one form for all)
exercises.explain: *gitmeli* + *-mi*, written on, the same for every person.

accept: You mustn't come into the house with your shoes on.
You mustn't go into the house with (your) shoes on.
You mustn't come into the house with shoes on.
[You shouldn't|One mustn't|One shouldn't|Don't] [come|go] into the house with (your) shoes on.
[You mustn't|You shouldn't|One mustn't|Don't] [come|go] into the house in (your) shoes.

exercises.prompt: You have to be quiet here. (a rule)
I had to take off my shoes.
exercises.explain: *çykarmaly* + *boldum*; **my shoes** as an object: *aýakgabymy* (*p* becomes *b* before a vowel).

exercises.question: Which sentence means **I needed a new key**?

why.1: The person who needs takes the dative: *maňa*. And *gerek* takes the past like an adjective: *gerekdi*.

exercises.explain: *Maňa* + *täze açar* + *gerekdi*, with the past of **to be** from [A2 unit 2](a2-u02).

accept: Don't you have to go to work?
Don't you need to go to work?
